key_insight: PMO-DDPG balances competing cobot welding objectives, reducing trajectory error by 66.4% and collision rate by 82.1% versus SAC in the evaluated settings.
engineering_relevance: Phase-aware trajectory planning could improve automotive spot-welding accuracy, safety, energy use, and throughput while retaining actor-only online inference.
method: Combines a deterministic actor with four critics for accuracy, smoothness, safety, and productivity.
Maps six normalized physical reward components to phase-dependent objectives across approach, alignment, welding, and retraction.
Uses a non-dominated policy archive for Pareto-guided policy selection.
evidence_signal: Simulation and industrial evaluation, including 100 industrial trials, reported 1.08 mm trajectory error, 1.2% collision rate, 3.87 s cycle time, and 94.6% success.
watch_item: Results are descriptive without formal significance testing; generalization beyond the evaluated simulation and industrial settings remains unestablished.
paper_title: Multi-objective deep deterministic policy gradient for cobot trajectory planning in automotive spot welding
